missing_supported_requirements.reason: The section discloses multiple climate metrics (Scopes 1–3, financed emissions, high-carbon exposure, internal carbon price) but does not clearly link metrics to each sustainability-related risk/opportunity that could reasonably be expected to affect prospects (i.e., no per-risk/opportunity mapping).

Metrics are presented, but the disclosure does not explicitly state which metrics are used to measure/monitor each identified sustainability-related risk or opportunity (no risk/opportunity-specific monitoring description).
Performance against targets is stated (e.g., progress % and 'On track'), but there is no analysis of trends or changes in performance (narrative trend analysis is missing).
No disclosure of whether targets were revised during the period; IFRS requires disclosure of revisions and explanations if revisions occurred (the section is silent).
The section does not state that metric definitions/calculations are consistent over time, nor does it describe any redefinitions/replacements and related application of B52 if applicable.

Comparative information for the preceding period is not provided for most disclosed amounts (e.g., Scope 1/2/Scope 3 business travel, high-carbon exposure, internal carbon prices, listed equity metrics). Only financed emissions (loans) includes 2022–2024.
The section does not state that GHG emissions are measured in accordance with the GHG Protocol (Corporate Standard 2004) or explain any alternative required method.

Some approach detail is provided for Scope 2 market-based and financed emissions (PCAF), but the overall measurement approach, key inputs and assumptions for Scope 1, Scope 2 (location-based), and Scope 3 business travel are not comprehensively described.
Reasons for choosing the measurement approaches/inputs/assumptions are not provided (e.g., why specific emission factors, why revenue proxy for listed equity).
No disclosure of changes to measurement approach/inputs/assumptions during the reporting period and reasons for changes (or an explicit statement that there were none).
No disaggregation of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions between the consolidated accounting group and other investees.
No disaggregation of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions for other investees excluded from the consolidated accounting group.
No disaggregation of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions for associates/joint ventures/unconsolidated subsidiaries (as applicable).

Location-based Scope 2 is disclosed, and contractual instruments are discussed at a high level, but the disclosure does not provide sufficient detail about contractual instruments necessary to inform understanding (e.g., nature/volume/coverage/quality of instruments, how they affect market-based figure).

Only two Scope 3 categories are disclosed (business travel and Category 15 financed emissions). The section does not disclose the categories included within the entity’s Scope 3 measure (i.e., whether Scope 3 is complete across categories or limited to selected categories).

required_fixes: Add explicit mapping of disclosed metrics to the relevant sustainability-related risks and opportunities (per risk/opportunity), or clearly state the climate-related risks/opportunities these metrics monitor.

Add comparative (preceding period) amounts for all metrics disclosed in 2024 (or, if truly impracticable, handle via IFRS S1 B54—but do not introduce 'impracticable' language unless supported elsewhere in the report).
State the GHG measurement standard used (GHG Protocol Corporate Standard 2004) or disclose the jurisdictional/exchange-required alternative method.

Expand GHG measurement approach disclosures: key inputs, assumptions, and (where applicable) limitations for Scope 1, Scope 2 (both bases), and Scope 3 business travel; include reasons for chosen approaches and disclose any changes during the period (or explicitly state none, if accurate and supported).

Provide required Scope 1 and Scope 2 disaggregation between consolidated accounting group and other investees (associates/JVs/unconsolidated subsidiaries/other investees), or clarify that there are no such investees if that is the case (only if supported).
For Scope 2 contractual instruments, provide decision-useful detail sufficient to understand the market-based figure (instrument types, coverage, and how they are reflected).
For Scope 3, clarify which Scope 3 categories are included in the entity’s Scope 3 measure (complete list or explicit statement that only selected categories are included).
Add trend/change analysis for performance against targets and disclose any target revisions and explanations (or explicitly state none, if accurate and supported).
ifrs_coverage_judge.summary: The section provides substantial climate metrics (Scopes 1–3, financed emissions, exposure, internal carbon pricing) and target progress, but it misses several supported IFRS S1/S2 requirements: comparative information for most metrics, explicit GHG Protocol basis, fuller methodology/assumptions and reasons, required Scope 1/2 disaggregation by investee type, clearer Scope 3 category coverage, and trend/revision disclosures for targets. No invented missing-data statements were found.

unsupported_claims.claim_or_excerpt: Scope 2 GHG emissions (location-based) in 2024 were 6,963.5 tCO₂e.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The claims register marks it supported, but the cited evidence paths do not include a specific KPI value for Scope 2 location-based emissions (no clear payload_path like reporting_kpis.scope2_location_2024_tco2e is provided in the evidence items shown). The evidence_sources listed for C005 appear unrelated to the numeric value.
unsupported_claims.fix_needed: Add a direct evidence item/path for the 2024 Scope 2 location-based value (e.g., reporting_kpis.scope2_location_2024_tco2e) and ensure it matches 6,963.5 tCO₂e.

unsupported_claims.claim_or_excerpt: Scope 3 (business travel) emissions in 2024 were 289.9 tCO₂e.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The claims register marks it supported, but the evidence_sources listed for C010 do not point to a business-travel KPI value; they appear to be generic metadata paths. No explicit evidence item for 289.9 tCO₂e is shown.
unsupported_claims.where_in_section: Selected Scope 3 category metric (business travel) table
unsupported_claims.fix_needed: Add a direct evidence item/path for Scope 3 business travel emissions in 2024 (e.g., reporting_kpis.scope3_business_travel_2024_tco2e) and ensure it matches 289.9 tCO₂e.

unsupported_claims.claim_or_excerpt: The financed emissions intensity target is validated by UNEP FI.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: Claim C026 has an empty evidence_sources list. No evidence item is provided showing UNEP FI validation.
unsupported_claims.where_in_section: Scope 3 Category 15 financed emissions intensity target (sectoral decarbonisation) — Third-party validation bullet
unsupported_claims.fix_needed: Provide an evidence source (e.g., targets[1].validation_body or an external assurance/validation reference) demonstrating UNEP FI validation, or remove/qualify the claim.

questionable_claims.claim_or_excerpt: Selected listed equity position metrics for 2024 are summarised below. (Market value / nominal amount with currency shown as EUR.)
questionable_claims.why_questionable: Evidence items indicate fields named market_value_meur and nominal_amount_meur (suggesting €m), while the table labels only 'Currency: EUR' without stating the unit magnitude (EUR vs €m). This creates unit ambiguity even if the numbers are evidenced.
questionable_claims.where_in_section: Financed emissions — listed equity (proxy input) table
questionable_claims.fix_needed: Explicitly label the unit for market value and nominal amount (e.g., '€m') and ensure consistency with the underlying data fields.

questionable_claims.claim_or_excerpt: High-carbon sector exposure was 35.5% (as a share of the relevant exposure measure used for this metric).
questionable_claims.why_questionable: The percentage is evidenced, but the denominator ('relevant exposure measure') is not defined in the section, limiting interpretability and auditability.
questionable_claims.fix_needed: Define the denominator/exposure measure (e.g., total credit exposure, EAD, on-balance-sheet exposure) and whether it is gross/net and which portfolios are included.

questionable_claims.claim_or_excerpt: Duplicate 'Investment decisions' internal carbon price entries (42.73 and 54.73) with different application flags.
questionable_claims.why_questionable: Both rows are labeled 'Investment decisions' but differ in price and applicability, which may be correct but is unclear without distinguishing sub-scopes (e.g., capex vs portfolio, short vs long-term shadow price).
questionable_claims.fix_needed: Clarify why there are two different prices for 'Investment decisions' (different business lines, time horizons, geographies, or decision contexts).

required_fixes: Add direct evidence references for 2024 Scope 2 location-based emissions (6,963.5 tCO₂e).
Add direct evidence references for 2024 Scope 3 business travel emissions (289.9 tCO₂e).
Provide evidence for UNEP FI validation of the financed emissions intensity target or revise/remove the validation claim.
Clarify units for listed equity market value/nominal amount (EUR vs €m) to match underlying data fields.
Define the denominator for the high-carbon sector exposure percentage.
Disambiguate the two 'Investment decisions' internal carbon price rows.
evidence_judge.summary: The section contains several quantitative and validation statements that are not adequately supported by the provided evidence mapping. In particular, the Scope 2 location-based value, Scope 3 business travel value, and UNEP FI validation lack direct evidence paths. Additional clarity is also needed on units (listed equity values), denominators (high-carbon exposure %), and duplicated internal carbon price categories.

voice_issues: Section generally uses neutral, standards-aligned voice, but does not consistently distinguish between first-person plural for entity actions and third-person for externally defined requirements (e.g., PCAF references are descriptive but not clearly framed as external requirements).
Some sentences are more explanatory than definitional (e.g., 'In plain language, the method attributes...'), which slightly departs from the preferred technical, audit-ready phrasing.
structure_issues: Headings are not numbered and do not follow the prescribed two-level hierarchy aligned to IFRS pillars (e.g., '## Reporting period and boundary' instead of '4.1 Reporting period and boundary').
Subsections often lack an explicit one-sentence purpose statement before details; some have it implicitly but not consistently formatted as a clear purpose lead-in.
Layered structure is only partially applied: there is overview plus tables, but limited closing 'connectivity' sentences linking to other sections or financial statements.
General sustainability metrics (IFRS S1) and climate-specific metrics (IFRS S2) are not explicitly separated or labelled as such.

Methodology, boundary, inputs, limitations, and governance are not consistently structured in the recommended sequence (boundary → inputs/sources → calculation steps → outputs/uses → limitations → governance/controls).
No explicit data currency/update cadence statement before presenting tables.
Tables are inserted without numbered captions (e.g., 'Table 4.1: Operational GHG emissions metrics') and are not explicitly referenced by number in the narrative.
wording_issues: Some phrasing is more narrative than definitional (e.g., 'In plain language, the method attributes a share...' rather than 'Financed emissions are calculated by attributing...').

Forward-looking or interpretive language is minimal but not clearly distinguished from current-period facts, estimates, and intentions (e.g., 'used to monitor progress' is fine but could be more explicitly framed as current use vs. future intent).
Preferred disclosure verbs (disclose, define, measure, calculate, present, classify, map, reconcile) are underused; the text relies more on generic verbs like 'provides' and 'applies'.

Assurance/validation references (e.g., 'Validated by SBTi', 'Validated by UNEP FI') are included without a clear assurance scope note or legend, which may be inconsistent with the evidence and traceability rules.
Some sentences are relatively long and multi-clause (e.g., Scope 2 market-based accounting description), which slightly departs from the short, precise, technical sentence preference.
table_figure_issues: Tables lack numbers and descriptive captions; they are presented as plain markdown tables without titles such as 'Table X: Metric register for operational emissions'.
Tables are not explicitly referenced in the narrative using their numbers, reducing traceability and audit-readiness.

Column structures do not follow the prescribed 'metrics register' pattern with definition, boundary, source type, internal source location, mapping to pillar/section, and assurance marker; they only show metric, value, unit (and sometimes exposure).

No explicit total rows or nested mini-tables are used where disaggregation is present (e.g., listed equity positions), and there is no explicit statement of whether the rows represent a complete set or a subset.
No assurance legend or footnotes are provided for methodological conventions, limitations, or data-quality notes; some methodology is embedded in narrative instead of structured footnotes.
Figures are not used, which is acceptable, but there are no visual anchors or captions to support PDF layout guidance in a long metrics section.
required_fixes: Introduce a numbered heading hierarchy aligned to IFRS pillars (e.g., '4 Metrics and Targets', '4.1 Reporting period and boundary', '4.2 Operational greenhouse gas emissions') and ensure consistent two-level structure.

Add explicit one-sentence purpose statements at the start of each subsection, clearly stating why the metrics/targets are disclosed and what they enable users to assess (e.g., 'This subsection discloses operational GHG emissions metrics used to monitor climate-related performance for the reporting period.').
Separate and label climate-specific metrics (IFRS S2) versus broader sustainability metrics (IFRS S1), or clarify that the section covers climate-related metrics only, as applicable.

Rework narrative blocks to follow the recommended sequence for complex metrics: boundary → inputs/sources → calculation steps → outputs/uses → limitations → governance/controls; for example, restructure the financed emissions and internal carbon pricing subsections accordingly.
Add a data currency and update cadence statement before the tables (e.g., 'Metrics are reported for the year ended 31 December 2024 and are updated annually in this report.').

Introduce numbered captions for each table (e.g., 'Table 4.1: Operational GHG emissions (Scopes 1 and 2)', 'Table 4.2: Scope 3 business travel emissions', 'Table 4.3: Financed emissions for corporate loans') and reference them explicitly in the narrative.

Expand table structures toward a metrics register format by adding columns for metric definition, boundary, source type (actual vs estimate), internal source location descriptor, mapping to IFRS pillar/section, and assurance marker where applicable.

Clarify assurance/validation references by adding an assurance scope note and a legend explaining any markers used, and distinguish between target validation (e.g., SBTi) and data assurance if both are present.

Tighten wording to use more standards-oriented verbs and definitional constructions (e.g., 'Financed emissions for corporate loans are calculated using...' instead of 'In plain language, the method attributes...'), and split long sentences into shorter, technical statements.

Add brief closing connectivity sentences for major subsections, linking metrics and targets to related narrative sections or financial statement areas (e.g., 'Refer to [Section: Strategy] for discussion of how these financed emissions metrics inform lending portfolio decisions.').

Ensure consistent terminology and capitalization (e.g., 'Scope 3 Category 15 financed emissions intensity target') and consider adding explicit status labels for any metrics or targets that are not applicable or not reported, even if none are currently missing, to demonstrate adherence to the missing-data protocol.

Review internal carbon pricing table for clarity and potential duplication (two 'Investment decisions' rows) and, if intentional, define the different application scopes more precisely in the narrative or table definition column.
style_judge.summary: The section is broadly aligned with the formal, neutral, audit-ready style and uses structured tables and technical language. However, it does not fully meet the approved authoring style due to missing numbered headings and table captions, limited use of metrics-register columns and assurance/traceability metadata, inconsistent application of the layered structure and methodology sequence, and underuse of standards-oriented verbs and definitional phrasing. With these structural and wording refinements, the section could be approved as an IFRS-style Metrics and Targets disclosure.
